headline: Peter Cardillo expects sticky but non-accelerating US CPI to keep the Fed on hold in September
reasoning: Cardillo forecasts a modest 0.1% increase in headline CPI and a 0.1% decrease in core CPI for the month, indicating inflation remains sticky and elevated but without meaningful acceleration. He believes this print will be sufficient to keep the Federal Reserve on hold at its September meeting. The key takeaway, in his view, is that there is no real re-acceleration in inflation.
quote: I think we're going to see a modest gains from last month. I'm looking for a one tenth of a percent increase in, um, in, uh, uh, headline inflation and in the core, uh, probably down zero one tenth of a percent. So it'll, it'll show that inflation remains sticky and elevated, but we're not seeing any real acceleration. And that's the key. And I think that puts, uh, the Fed's on hold for September.

headline: Peter Cardillo believes US equity indices can continue moving higher on the back of corporate tax cuts boosting earnings
reasoning: Cardillo argues it is very difficult to call a market top when earnings remain strong coming off what he describes as a great earnings season. He believes the indices have room to continue moving higher, though at a slower pace than previously seen. He attributes the earnings strength primarily to corporate tax cuts reducing companies' tax burdens rather than an aggressively strong underlying economy, noting that lower taxes are directly adding to the bottom line of corporate America.
quote: In terms of stocks, you know, look we're just coming off of a great earnings season. And um, and until that changes, it's going to be very difficult to call a market top. I believe we can continue to move higher.
